title: Ezekiel Bible Quiz - Chapter 3
description: Ten questions on Ezekiel 3: eating the scroll, the hard forehead, Tel Aviv and the watchman over the house of Israel.

questions.text: What did the scroll taste like when he ate it?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 3:3 says that when he ate the scroll it was as sweet as honey in his mouth.

answers.text: As sweet as honey
As bitter as gall
Like dry ashes
Like fresh oil

questions.text: According to verse 5, to which kind of people is he not sent?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 3:5-6 says he is not sent to a people of a strange speech and a hard language, but to the house of Israel.

answers.text: To the house of Israel in their own land
To a people of a strange speech and a hard language
To the captives who live by the river Chebar
To kings and princes of a far country

questions.text: Why does the voice say the house of Israel will not listen to him?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 3:7 says they will not listen to him because they will not listen to God, for all the house of Israel are obstinate and hard-hearted.

answers.text: Because they cannot understand his speech or language
Because they already have another prophet among them
Because they will not listen to God, being obstinate and hard-hearted
Because their own elders have forbidden them to listen

questions.text: What has God made his forehead like?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 3:9 says God made his forehead as a diamond, harder than flint, and told him not to be afraid of them.

answers.text: As bronze, harder than iron
As a wall of hewn stone
As a shield of thick wood
As a diamond, harder than flint

questions.text: What did he hear behind him when the Spirit lifted him up?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 3:12 says he heard behind him the voice of a great rushing, saying, "Blessed be Yahweh's glory from his place."

answers.text: The sound of a trumpet calling the captives out to battle
A great rushing voice saying, "Blessed be Yahweh's glory from his place"
The weeping of the women of Zion in the city streets
A voice telling him to flee away from that place

questions.text: In what state did he go when the Spirit took him away?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 3:14 says he went in bitterness, in the heat of his spirit, and Yahweh's hand was strong on him.

answers.text: In bitterness, in the heat of his spirit
Rejoicing greatly in his heart
In silence and in great fear
As one asleep in a deep dream

questions.text: Where did he come to the captives, and how long did he sit overwhelmed among them?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 3:15 says he came to them of the captivity at Tel Aviv, by the river Chebar, and sat there overwhelmed among them seven days.

answers.text: At Tel Aviv, for three days
In Babylon, for forty days
In Jerusalem, for seven days
At Tel Aviv, for seven days

questions.text: What has God made him to the house of Israel?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 3:17 says God has made him a watchman to the house of Israel, who must hear the word from God's mouth and warn them.

answers.text: A judge
A priest
A watchman
A shepherd

questions.text: What does Yahweh say will happen if the watchman gives the wicked man no warning and that man dies in his iniquity?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 3:18 says the wicked man will die in his iniquity, but God will require his blood at the watchman's hand.

answers.text: The wicked man will live out all of his days
God will require the dead man's blood at the watchman's hand
No one at all will be held to account for it
Another prophet will be sent to warn that man

questions.text: What does Yahweh say he will do so that the man cannot correct the rebellious house?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 3:26 says God will make his tongue stick to the roof of his mouth so that he will be mute and unable to correct them.

answers.text: Take away his visions for many days to come
Shut him out of the city of the captives
Send him far away from the captives by the river
Make his tongue stick to the roof of his mouth so he is mute
